reviews.fact_before: when a metal rusts , that metal becomes orange on the surface
reviews.correction: Rust is a corrosion product of iron and iron-containing materials and often looks reddish brown or orange. Corrosion of other metals does not necessarily produce rust or an orange surface; copper patina is a different corrosion product.
reviews.reason: The characteristic appearance of iron rust is generalized to metals and jewelry of unspecified composition.

reviews.correction: Many materials expand when their temperature rises under suitable conditions, but expansion is not an unconditional result of adding heat. Liquid water contracts when warmed from about 0 to 4 degrees Celsius at ordinary pressure. The material, temperature interval, and constraints must be specified.
reviews.reason: A common response is treated as a universal rule and used in unrelated causal chains.

reviews.fact_before: condensing means changing from a gas into a liquid by reducing heat energy
reviews.correction: Condensation is the change from gas to liquid. Cooling can cause it, but pressure also affects phase equilibrium: below the critical temperature, suitable compression can condense a vapor without reducing its temperature. Condensation releases latent heat rather than requiring that the temperature fall throughout the phase change.
reviews.reason: The source conflates energy transfer, temperature, and the definition of a phase change.

reviews.fact_before: a seismometer is used to measure the strength or magnitude of an earthquake
reviews.correction: A seismometer records ground motion over time. Seismic records are analyzed to estimate earthquake magnitude; magnitude is distinct from the shaking intensity experienced at a particular location. A seismometer does not directly read a universal one-to-ten earthquake grade.
reviews.reason: The simplified instrument description is used to equate ground motion, magnitude, and intensity.

reviews.fact_before: volcanic ash in the atmosphere decreases the temperature by blocking the sun
reviews.correction: Volcanic ash can reduce sunlight locally for a limited time, but much ash falls out relatively quickly. Sustained cooling after some large eruptions is mainly associated with sulfate aerosols formed from sulfur dioxide in the stratosphere. An eruption does not automatically produce a specified decrease in temperature.
reviews.reason: The source omits the distinction between short-lived ash and longer-lived sulfate aerosols and generalizes across eruptions.

reviews.fact_before: All traffic vehicles are Air Planes.
reviews.correction: Vehicles include cars, buses, trucks, and other forms of transport as well as aircraft. Airplanes are one type of vehicle, not every traffic vehicle.
reviews.reason: The source replaces a broad category with one of its members.

reviews.fact_before: Navigation is done by compass only.
reviews.correction: A compass can support navigation, but it is not the only method. Satellite-based GPS also provides positioning and navigation services.
reviews.reason: An exclusive method claim ignores established alternative navigation technology.

reviews.fact_before: Heat is the energy of moving molecules.
reviews.correction: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Microscopic molecular motion contributes to internal energy, but stored microscopic energy is not itself heat.
reviews.reason: The source equates microscopic motion or its energy with the physical definition of heat.

reviews.fact_before: Heat is caused by molecules moving.
reviews.correction: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Microscopic molecular motion contributes to internal energy, but stored microscopic energy is not itself heat.
reviews.reason: The source equates microscopic motion or its energy with the physical definition of heat.

reviews.fact_before: Earthquakes are measured on a scale of 1 to 10.
reviews.correction: Earthquake magnitude is logarithmic and is not confined to a one-to-ten rating. Small earthquakes can have negative magnitudes. Magnitude must also be distinguished from local shaking intensity.
reviews.reason: The stated fixed numeric scale is false and propagates into a claim about the instrument range.

reviews.fact_before: When a gas condenses to form a liquid it absorbs heat.
reviews.correction: When a vapor condenses at its phase-transition conditions, it releases latent heat to its surroundings. Vaporization is the reverse change and absorbs heat.
reviews.reason: The source reverses the sign of heat transfer for condensation.

reviews.correction: Black sand is not synonymous with airborne volcanic ash. Some Hawaiian black sand forms when lava is rapidly cooled and fragmented by seawater. Sand on a beach cannot inherit atmospheric effects merely because its material has a volcanic origin.
reviews.reason: The source conflates a beach sediment with suspended ash and transfers an atmospheric effect to it.
